en: Dark, towering cumulonimbus clouds with flat anvil-shaped tops often indicate an approaching thunderstorm.
The rich, dark soil around Mayon Volcano is highly fertile because it contains weathered volcanic ash.
Pumice is a light, porous volcanic rock that contains trapped gas bubbles allowing it to float on water.
Banana plants release large amounts of water vapor into the air through their leaves via transpiration.
The Sun appears much larger and brighter than other stars because it is much closer to Earth.
The star Polaris, located at the end of the Little Dipper's handle, always points directly north.
During a full moon, the entire sunlit side of the Moon faces Earth, forming a complete circle.
The Valley Fault System in Metro Manila can produce strong earthquakes when its underground rocks suddenly slip.
Spring tides occur when the Sun, Earth, and Moon align, causing higher high tides in coastal areas.
The amihan or northeast monsoon brings cool, dry air to the Philippines between November and February.
Stalactites in Puerto Princesa Subterranean River form drop by drop as mineral-rich water drips from cave ceilings.
Lahars are fast-moving mudflows made of volcanic ash and rainwater that travel down the slopes of Mount Pinatubo.
